extracted.intended_audience: Patent applicants/representatives and USPTO patent examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for conducting and documenting interviews between patent applicants/representatives and USPTO examiners during patent prosecution to advance prosecution and reach agreement. Covers preparation, conduct, timing, topics, and required documentation (PTOL-413/413A).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use an Agenda (preferably PTOL-413A); review record in advance; consult with SPE or Primary if needed; consider any suggested claim language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare an agenda (PTOL-413A) and review the file history before the interview; have proposed claim language ready if applicable; consult supervisory personnel when needed to ensure productive discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperation
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep an open mind; maintain a positive attitude; seek common ground; work on claim language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approach interviews collaboratively rather than adversarially; emphasize finding mutual agreement and constructive amendment of claim language where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Active listening (eye contact, body language, proper tone and volume); stay focused on the agenda; seek common understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use active listening skills and clear verbal/nonverbal communication to keep the discussion on-topic and ensure both parties understand positions and issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome (what constitutes an effective interview)
rubrics_metrics.description: Issues are resolved, reduced or clarified; better understanding of applicant’s position, examiner’s position, and claim interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An effective interview produces clarified issues and mutual understanding that can materially affect prosecution strategy and next actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefits of Interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Leads to better understanding of the invention, applicant’s position, examiner’s position, and claim interpretation; advances/promotes compact prosecution; increases chance of disposal in next Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews statistically increase the likelihood of a disposal in the next Office action (presentation shows higher disposal percentages when interviews occur); use interviews to streamline prosecution and narrow disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Challenges to Effective Interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Lack of agenda (can become a 'fishing' expedition); unprepared party (applicant/representative or examiner); time concerns such as scheduling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid unstructured conversations by providing an agenda and preparing participants; be mindful of scheduling constraints and keep the meeting focused.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested Sequence for an Effective Interview
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant/Representative explains invention; discuss how inventive concepts are (or are not) set forth in the claim language; discuss prior art and rejections; discuss any proposed language (from either party); establish common ground (each topic — agree or not).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow this sequence to structure the conversation: start with the invention overview, move to claim-language alignment with inventive concepts, address prior art/rejections, propose and discuss amendments, and record areas of agreement/disagreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reaching Agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Possible outcomes include allowance (not the only agreement), reduction in number of rejections, resolution of other issues/formalities, simply 'agree-to-disagree' on topics, and deciding next steps (Allowance, Abandonment, CIP, RCE…).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use interviews to clarify positions and decide concrete next steps; agreement can be partial and still useful for prosecution strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview Requests — required content and approach
rubrics_metrics.description: When requesting an interview, inquire about the purpose/intent; request an agenda (PTOL-413A); indicate any proposed amendments; see MPEP 713 (Interviews).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame interview requests with a clear purpose and attach or request an agenda (use PTOL-413A); include proposed amendments to focus the discussion and cite MPEP guidance as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: When an Interview Can Be Helpful
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews may be helpful before first action (see MPEP 713.02), after first action, and after final (see MPEP 713.09) depending on circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider interviews at various prosecution stages; note specific MPEP sections for guidance on timing and scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Before First Action Interview Program (pilot)
rubrics_metrics.description: A pilot program exists for Before First Action interviews in Business Method and Electrical Technology Center areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether an application qualifies for the pilot; use the pilot to potentially shape claims before a first Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: When an Examiner May Deny an Interview
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners may deny interviews after final action, particularly after an Appeal Brief has been filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that the ability to secure an interview can be limited late in prosecution; plan interviews earlier where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Granting Interviews — Examiner expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners are instructed to be accessible, flexible, adjust work schedule within reason, use multiple formats (phone / in-person), and find a common time and place that works; applicants/representatives are asked to reciprocate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both parties should be willing to accommodate reasonable scheduling and format requests to facilitate the interview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typical Interview Topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Overview of the invention; state of the art; claim interpretation; prior art used in rejections; language in proposed amendment; 35 U.S.C. 101; 35 U.S.C. 112(1), 112(2), 112(6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the interview to address substantive prosecution issues, including statutory grounds for rejection and specific claim language changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documenting Interviews — Interview Summary (PTOL-413)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interview Summary (PTOL-413) should include details enough to clarify the record, claim limitations discussed, claim interpretation issues, details of proposed amendment, agenda items, topics resolved (agreed to), and topics unresolved (not agreed to).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete a PTOL-413 summary after substantive discussions to ensure the file reflects what was discussed and any agreements or unresolved issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of an 'Interview' and Off-the-Record Guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: A discussion is an 'interview' if it touches on the merits of the case (claim language, prior art analysis, clarification of a rejection, etc.). Do not prosecute 'off the record.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive merit discussions must be documented; follow MPEP 713.04 and procedures for transmission/recording (see MPEP 502.01 for fax, 502.02 for e-sig, and 502.03 for email). Avoid informal, undocumented prosecution activities.
